title: What the Galápagos Tortoise outlasts

is_this_you.pressure: When it gets loud, you draw in and wait. You have outlasted worse than this, and you remember it.
is_this_you.love: You love by being in the same place every morning. You trust anyone who notices.
is_this_you.cost: You hold up other people's monuments so steadily that they forget anyone is underneath.

opener.text: The Book of Rites names four sacred creatures, 麟鳳龜龍 (lín fèng guī lóng): the lin, the feng, the tortoise and the dragon [s7]. It calls them the four numinous ones [s7]. The tortoise and the dragon sit side by side in that list. You were born a Taurus in a Dragon year. The old book put your two halves together long before you arrived. It took its time. So will you.

howto: Three parts. There is no hurry.

tabs.label: The long view
tabs.intro: Earth on Earth, and plenty of time.

rows.text: Taurus is fixed Earth, ruled by Venus, the sign that stays with a goal and follows through [s1] [s2]. The Dragon is yang Earth, brave and willing to take risks [s3] [s4]. So you are Earth twice over. The Taurus in you wants one good hillside. The Dragon in you wants that hillside to mean something.

A Galápagos tortoise reaches maturity at around 40 years in the wild [s5]. Wild tortoises are thought to live past 100 [s5]. Each morning it basks for an hour or two after dawn before it goes to feed [s5]. You start late and warm up slowly. Whatever you build after that has a century in it.
Males settle rank by how high they can raise their necks [s5]. Nobody runs. Nobody bites first. You win the same way, by rising to your full height and waiting for the other one to understand.

Taurus is stubborn, with a fierce temper once roused [s1] [s2]. Dragons can easily get into conflicts [s4]. So you pull in first and stand your ground completely after. Name the hurt before the shell shuts.

tabs.label: What you carry
tabs.intro: Stored water, old paths, a heavy stone.

rows.text: A Galápagos tortoise can last up to a year without food or water [s5]. It drinks deeply and stores the water in its bladder [s5]. You get through dry stretches on what you put away when nobody was looking. When the rain returns, you hardly mention it.

Big adults walk up to about 10 kilometres uphill as the dry season starts, then back down when the rains green the lowlands [s6]. They travel along paths their kind has used for generations [s5] [s6]. You keep to the old routes too. You time them by the weather, never the calendar.

Land, property and conservation suit you. So do archives, heritage work and anything made of stone. The Dragon's career lists name engineer and architect [s4], and Taurus gives you the patience for buildings that take years.

tabs.label: Who walks with you
tabs.intro: Three who keep your pace. One who wants to hurry you.
tabs.love_lead: In love you show up in the same spot every morning and call that a promise. You need someone who can wait out a cool dawn beside you without asking what is wrong. Three animals sit easily with you.

easy.why: The Andean Condor (Capricorn, Rooster year) is your secret friend, since the Rooster and the Dragon make a Six Harmonies pair, and Capricorn is the third Earth sign [s3] [s1].
The Aardwolf (Taurus, Rat year) shares your trine of Rat, Dragon and Monkey and was born under your sign [s3].
The New Caledonian Crow (Virgo, Monkey year) closes that trine, with Virgo's Earth beside yours [s3] [s1].

hard.why: The hard one is the Tasmanian Devil (Scorpio, Dog year): the Dog clashes with the Dragon, and Scorpio sits opposite Taurus [s3] [s1].

story.text: One of the dragon's sons, 贔屭 (bìxì), wears a tortoise's shell [s8]. Since at least the late Han, stone carvings of him have carried memorial steles on their backs [s8]. Dictionaries gloss his name as strong, able to bear great weight [s8]. He holds up the record and never asks to be read.

closing: Hold the stone steady. Long after the carvers are gone, someone will still be reading it.
